Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which organ is mostly made up of nerve tissue. The options given are brain, liver, skin, and stomach. I remember from biology that the brain is a major organ involving nerves, but I'm not 100% sure. Let me think through this step by step.

First, I know that the body has different types of tissues: muscle, epithelial, nerve, and connective. Nerve tissue is specifically related to the nervous system. So, the brain is part of the central nervous system, which includes the brain and the spinal cord. That makes sense because the brain processes information and controls various functions.

The liver is an organ involved in digestion and blood processing. I don't recall the liver being primarily nerve tissue. In fact, the liver has a mix of tissues, including connective and maybe some supportive cells, but not predominantly nerve tissue.

Skin is an epithelial tissue, covering the body to protect against external factors. So, skin isn't made up of nerves; instead, it's more about protection and sensation, which comes from nerve endings embedded in it.

The stomach is part of the digestive system. It has lining tissues that are epithelial, and muscles for churning food, which are muscle tissue. So, the stomach doesn't consist mostly of nerve tissue either.

Putting this together, the brain is the organ that's made up mostly of nerve tissue. It's responsible for the central nervous system functions, so it makes sense as the correct answer. I don't see any errors in this reasoning, so I think the answer is correct.
</think>

1. Yes.
2. Reason: The brain is the organ composed mostly of nerve tissue, as it is part of the central nervous system responsible for processing and controlling various bodily functions. The other options (liver, skin, stomach) do not consist primarily of nerve tissue.
